# Contact-row limits with boundary defects and retained gradient labels

This is an exact limit theorem for the actual logarithmic contact rows. It
retains boundary concentration in dm/L instead of assuming uniform
integrability. The added uniform unscaled L and marked-value bounds are
supplied in the scalar-selected application by Sections 3--4 of
`candidate b4f092ee1bb5a205` and the
attained scalar selection in
`candidate 281b285239e28b38`.

The theorem does not prove that deepest-source geometry or ordinary physical
stress eliminates the boundary defect. Slab's actual truncated-triangle
certificate shows that the parameter and source-core bounds alone do not.
No Gamma payment is inferred.

## 1. Exact sequence and hypotheses

Let P be finite and K_z^j converge in Hausdorff distance to positive convex
K_z. Retain a common outer radius R, positive lower volumes, and uniform
inradii. Write dm_j for mixed volume, M_j its mass, and dm,M for their limits.

Let L_j be positive finite-PL jointly concave parameters, log-normalized on
the sampled fibers. Suppose

    max_Sj L_j<=L_*,  L_*>=1.                         (1)

There is a fixed finite source label set i=1,...,m, with marks
Y_ij=(p_i,y_ij) converging to Y_i, uniformly interior in their own fibers,
and values L_ij=L_j(Y_ij) satisfying

    L_ij>=l_*>0.                                     (2)

The labels may include weights tending to zero. Each current weight sigma_ij
is positive, sum_i sigma_ij=1, and the ACTUAL contact probability rows rho_ij
satisfy

    E_rhoij w=Y_ij,   E_rhoij L_j=L_ij,
    sum_i (sigma_ij/L_ij)rho_ij =dm_j/(M_j L_j).       (3)

Equivalently, their original-volume reweightings are

    d bar_rho_ij=(L_j/L_ij)d rho_ij,
    sum_i sigma_ij bar_rho_ij=dm_j/M_j.               (4)

These are genuine rows with source contact, not merely measures having
chosen first moments. The full physical dual need not be invoked for the
measure-limit theorem. When it is invoked, it must be the same certificate.

## 2. Bounded touching planes and uniform sampled convergence

At every source with positive weight, the contact theorem gives a unique
continuous gradient c_ij of L_j. An own ball of radius r_s implies

    |c_ij|/L_ij<=1/r_s.

Thus (1) uniformly bounds these continuous slopes. Choose one sampled
affine majorant A_ij>=L_j touching at Y_ij with that continuous slope.
Its base slope can be chosen uniformly bounded by the finite support LP:
the data max_Kzj(L_j-c_ij.X) are bounded, the base matrix is fixed, and
the minimum-norm feasible base slope is bounded by the finitely many
independent active-row inverses. This is the already audited sampled
touching-majorant construction; no ambient supergradient at a boundary
base is presumed.

Put V_j=min_i A_ij. The old global certificate gives

    mean_Sj log(V_j/L_j)
          <=sum_i sigma_ij log[V_j(Y_ij)/L_ij]=0.

Since V_j>=L_j on S_j, equality follows, and continuity gives V_j=L_j on
every sampled fiber, including its boundary. We may therefore use this
finite-plane representative in all the measures (3)--(4). It need not
agree with a previously chosen extension at nonsampled bases.

Equivalently this conclusion follows directly from (3), without invoking
the global logarithmic inequality: each A_ij satisfies E_rhoij A_ij=L_ij
=E_rhoij L_j, so A_ij=L_j on that row. Hence V_j=L_j on every row, and
their positive-density mixture gives equality throughout the sampled fibers.

After a subsequence all plane coefficients converge. Consequently

    L_j=min_i A_ij -> L=min_i A_i                     (5)

uniformly on a common compact ambient bounding set. Each A_i is nonnegative
on the limiting canonical hull. Also L_ij tends to L_i=L(Y_i)>=l_*.

For clarity, the limit L is positive on EVERY sampled fiber interior, not
only at its sources. Let m_zj=max_Kzj L_j. Since log normalization implies
sum_z V_zj log m_zj>=0 and all maxima are at most L_*, positive lower
fiber volumes give a uniform lower bound for every m_zj. Nonnegative
concavity then gives

    L_j(z,X)>=m_zj dist(X,boundary K_zj)/(2R).

The uniform boundary-layer estimate O(s) makes log L_j uniformly integrable.
Thus log normalization passes to the limit, mean_S log L=0, and L is
positive in each sampled interior. Its zero set

    Z={w in S:L(w)=0}                                 (6)

is a mixed-volume-null subset of the sampled boundaries. Because L is a
finite minimum of nonnegative affine functions, Z lies in the finite union
of their exposed zero faces. No assertion that Z is a single face is made.

## 3. The full limiting martingale includes a positive boundary defect

After a further subsequence sigma_ij tends to sigma_i, and every rho_ij has
a weak probability limit rho_i on the limiting sampled bodies. Sources
with sigma_i=0 may be discarded in the formulas below. Compact support and
(5) allow passage of BOTH moments:

    E_rhoi w=Y_i,  E_rhoi L=L_i.                      (7)

The measures nu_j=dm_j/(M_j L_j) have bounded total mass, because (3) gives

    nu_j(S_j)=sum_i sigma_ij/L_ij<=1/l_*.

Their actual weak limit is

    nu=sum_i (sigma_i/L_i)rho_i.                      (8)

It satisfies the exact measure identity

    L nu=dm/M.                                       (9)

Indeed L_j nu_j=dm_j/M_j, and uniform convergence of L_j together with
bounded nu_j mass permits passage against any continuous test function.
Equivalently, first restrict to a compact region where L>0 and pass its
bounded reciprocal density. It follows that

    nu=dm/(M L)+zeta,
    zeta>=0,  support(zeta) subset Z.                 (10)

The integral of 1/L in (10) is finite, by Fatou or by domination by nu.
The measure zeta need not be atomic; the word defect includes concentration
on any zero face. It is NOT licensed to delete zeta from the martingale.

The joint measure

    pi=sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) delta_Yi tensor rho_i

is an actual martingale from mu=sum_i (sigma_i/L_i)delta_Yi to nu. Its
zeroth and first moment equations are

    zeta(S)=sum_i sigma_i/L_i-(1/M)integral_S 1/L dm,
    integral w d zeta
       =sum_i (sigma_i/L_i)Y_i-(1/M)integral_S w/L dm. (11)

These identities retain the full base and continuous moments. The right
side of the first equation is nonnegative, and both differences are
determined by the SAME limiting rows. They are not free corrections.

Every limiting row still touches every active affine majorant of L at its
source. If A>=L touches at Y_i, affine barycenter preservation and (7) give

    E_rhoi(A-L)=A(Y_i)-L_i=0.

Since the integrand is nonnegative, A=L rho_i-almost everywhere. In
particular its part on Z is supported on the exposed face A=0. Base
barycenters also keep the entire row in the minimal base face of p_i.

## 4. Original-volume rows pass without the defect

Define

    d bar_rho_i=(L/L_i)d rho_i.

By (7) these are probabilities. Uniform convergence in (5) and (2) proves
the weak convergence bar_rho_ij to bar_rho_i, and (4) gives

    sum_i sigma_i bar_rho_i=dm/M.                     (12)

The defect on Z contributes ZERO to (12), since L=0 there. This does not
make the original-volume rows martingales. Let A_i be any active affine
majorant at Y_i, with full base/continuous gradient a_i. Since L=A_i on
the row and E_rhoi w=Y_i,

    E_barrhoi w-Y_i=Cov(rho_i) a_i/L_i.               (13)

Boundary concentration is included in this covariance. Formula (13), not
the tilted mean Y_i, is the retained original-row mean. In particular the
two row couplings cannot be identified after taking limits.

## 5. Positive source gradients and labeled defects

For sigma_i>0, (12) makes bar_rho_i absolutely continuous with respect to
mixed volume, and it has total mass one. If two active majorants at Y_i
had different continuous gradients, their equality hyperplane would be
volume-null in EVERY sampled fiber. But the preceding contact equality
would support bar_rho_i there, a contradiction. Thus every positive
limiting source again has a unique continuous gradient c_i.

At mixed-volume-a.e. target point in that row, L is differentiable in X
and grad_X L=c_i. The boundary part, however, may land at a crease where
there is no single gradient. Keep its source label explicitly:

    zeta_i=(sigma_i/L_i) rho_i restricted_to Z,
    zeta=sum_i zeta_i.                               (14)

For every function chi on the finite set of surviving labels,

    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) chi(c_i)(1,Y_i)
      =(1/M)integral_S chi(grad_X L)(1,w)/L dm
                      +sum_i chi(c_i)integral_Z (1,w)d zeta_i. (15)

This is the exact limiting TILTED label identity, including its defect.
It follows either from the labeled rows or by compactifying the joint
gradient-label measures. Coalescing gradient labels may simply be merged.

Multiplication by L removes the boundary term and gives the unchanged
ORIGINAL-volume label masses

    sum_i sigma_i chi(c_i)
           =(1/M)integral_S chi(grad_X L) dm.          (16)

For original first moments the covariance terms must still be retained:

    (1/M)integral chi(grad_X L) w dm
       =sum_i sigma_i chi(c_i)
                         [Y_i+Cov(rho_i)a_i/L_i].     (17)

For example chi(c)=|c| in (15) gives

    sum_i sigma_i |c_i|/L_i
       =(1/M)integral |grad_X L|/L dm
                              +sum_i |c_i| zeta_i(Z). (18)

There is no unproved lower-semicontinuity equality deleting the last term.
The earlier vanishing of the SCALED physical logarithm multiplies such
terms by a coefficient tending to zero and does not imply zeta=0.

## 6. What actual deepestness and the ordinary stress do and do not add

In the scalar-selected joint-minimum application, the limiting Y_i are
ordinary deepest marks and the ordinary cap stress is supplied by
`candidate 714f69e684c396b1`.
These are additional geometric data. None of equations (7)--(18) turns them
into a proved exclusion of zeta. In particular the cap stress lives on
surface area, while zeta is a possible weak defect of reciprocal VOLUME
density on a zero face; matching their dimensions or supports does not
identify their marginals or weights.

The counterexample in
`candidate 1b1d5e313c1943d1`
has one actual contact row with a uniform interior source ball, uniform
L_max and positive marked value, yet a nonzero point defect at a limiting
triangle vertex. Its source is not asserted deepest or physically stationary.
It therefore refutes automatic uniform integrability under Sections 1--2,
but does not settle whether the extra joint-minimum geometry rules it out.

The rigorously closed alternative is to retain zeta and its labeled
moments exactly as above. No false martingale for dm/(M L) alone is claimed.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_contact_row_boundary_defect_identities_defect_transport.py`
checks the scalar moment/reweighting identities on exact finite contact
rows with genuine zero-L target atoms. Those finite checks illustrate the
identities, not the convex-body existence theorem or a deepestness claim.
